Tom / Sarah — quick operational response with the enumerated subprocessors and evidence pointers below:

- Managed GPU provider (EU pool) — May process request payloads in memory for inference. When Dedicated EU-only is provisioned, access is restricted by tenancy and we require contractual subprocessor clauses. No persistent copies are kept by default; ephemeral caches (KV) live in memory and are zeroed on node termination.
- Observability vendor (metrics + traces) — receives aggregated traces and error payloads; we redact full request payloads by default, but non-redacted traces can be forwarded only under debug requested by customer. They do not store raw request bodies persistently (90-day telemetry retention).
- Logging S3 (long-term logs) — persistent, encrypted at rest; we only ship metadata and truncated logs by default; full request bodies are not exported unless customer enables debug shipping.
- Metrics ingestion (third-party) — aggregated numeric metrics only; no payloads.

Attachments included: subprocessor_evidence.zip (sample contractual clauses and access control screenshots). Also: link to SOC2 snapshot: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2/2026 (access-controlled).

On your specific Q about Dedicated EU-only: if you provision Dedicated EU-only capacity and opt-in to EU residency for backups/metrics, the in-scope processing will remain inside EU boundaries and that materially reduces the transfer risk. However:

- Some ancillary control-plane signals (billing, billing IDs, and aggregated usage metrics) may still flow through our control plane which is hosted in multi-region; these can be minimized but not wholly eliminated unless you opt into a private control plane (Redwood Private).
- For that reason, we generally still execute SCCs as a baseline even when Dedicated EU processing is used, unless you sign an addendum that scopes the contract to EU-only processing and accepts our proposed control-plane mitigations.

Procurement note: Dedicated EU capacity pricing guidance attached in the call invite; rough delta is +30–45% of standard hosted rates depending on commit. Final quote requires throughput estimates.

Let me know if you want an itemized DocuSign packet and who should be the signatories.

-Kim

Attachments: subprocessor_evidence.zip
